statement: Vaccines cause autism.
explanation_short: Large studies have found no link between vaccines and autism.
explanation_long: Many large studies across several countries have found no link between vaccines and autism. Autism is a lifelong neurodevelopmental difference.

statement: ADHD can continue into adulthood.
explanation_short: ADHD often continues into adulthood.
explanation_long: ADHD often starts in childhood and, for many people, continues into adulthood. Symptoms can look different as people get older.

statement: People with dyslexia are less intelligent.
explanation_short: Dyslexia has nothing to do with intelligence.
explanation_long: Dyslexia is a difference in how the brain processes written language. It is unrelated to intelligence, and many people with dyslexia excel in their fields.

statement: Autistic people can have very different strengths and support needs.
explanation_short: Autism is a spectrum; no two autistic people are the same.
explanation_long: Autism is a spectrum. Some autistic people need a lot of daily support and others need very little, and each person has their own strengths.

statement: ADHD is caused by bad parenting or a lack of discipline.
explanation_short: ADHD is a neurodevelopmental condition, not a parenting failure.
explanation_long: Research points to genetics and brain development, not parenting or lack of willpower, as the main factors in ADHD.

statement: Autistic people don't feel empathy.
explanation_short: Many autistic people feel deeply but may show it differently.
explanation_long: Autistic people can care deeply about others. They may express feelings or read social cues differently, which is often mistaken for a lack of empathy.

statement: Neurodiversity means human brains naturally work in different ways.
explanation_short: Neurodiversity is the idea that brain differences are natural variation.
explanation_long: Neurodiversity describes the natural range of differences in how people think, learn and process information. It includes autism, ADHD, dyslexia and more.

statement: Children grow out of dyslexia.
explanation_short: Dyslexia is lifelong, but the right support helps a lot.
explanation_long: Dyslexia is lifelong. With good teaching, tools and accommodations, people with dyslexia learn strategies that work for them.

statement: Girls and women with ADHD are often diagnosed later than boys.
explanation_short: ADHD in girls and women is often missed or diagnosed late.
explanation_long: ADHD in girls and women can look less 'hyperactive' and more inattentive, so it is often recognised later.

statement: Stimming, like rocking or fidgeting, can help autistic people self-regulate.
explanation_short: Stimming helps many autistic people manage feelings and senses.
explanation_long: Repetitive movements or sounds (stimming) can help autistic people cope with stress, excitement or sensory overload. It usually isn't something to stop.

statement: If you can't see a disability, it isn't real.
explanation_short: Many disabilities are invisible but very real.
explanation_long: Conditions like chronic pain, hearing loss, epilepsy, diabetes or mental health conditions can be disabling without being visible.

statement: Many disabilities, such as chronic pain or hearing loss, aren't visible.
explanation_short: Many disabilities are hidden.
explanation_long: A large share of disabilities are not obvious to others. That's why it's important not to judge whether someone 'looks disabled'.

statement: It's helpful to start pushing someone's wheelchair without asking.
explanation_short: Always ask first; a wheelchair is part of someone's personal space.
explanation_long: A wheelchair is part of a person's personal space. Ask if they would like help, and follow their lead on how.
source_name: UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities

statement: When someone uses a sign language interpreter, you should speak directly to the person, not the interpreter.
explanation_short: Talk to the person, not the interpreter.
explanation_long: Look at and speak to the person you're talking with. The interpreter is there to relay the conversation.
source_name: UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities

statement: It's fine to pet a guide dog because guide dogs are friendly.
explanation_short: Guide and assistance dogs are working; don't distract them.
explanation_long: Assistance dogs are working. Petting or calling them can distract them from keeping their handler safe. Ask the handler first.

statement: Asking 'Would you like help?' and accepting 'no' is good etiquette.
explanation_short: Offer help, then respect the answer.
explanation_long: People with disabilities are the experts on their own needs. Offering help is kind; respecting a 'no' is just as important.
source_name: UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities

statement: Mental health conditions can be disabilities.
explanation_short: Psychosocial disabilities are recognised internationally.
explanation_long: The UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities includes long-term mental impairments that, with barriers, limit full participation.
source_name: UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities

statement: Someone who uses a wheelchair can never stand or walk.
explanation_short: Many wheelchair users can stand or walk short distances.
explanation_long: People use wheelchairs for many reasons, such as fatigue, pain or balance. Some can stand or walk a little, and that doesn't mean they don't need the chair.

statement: Speaking louder and slower helps every person with a disability understand you.
explanation_short: Speak normally unless the person asks you to change.
explanation_long: Most people don't need you to change how you speak. If someone does, they'll tell you what helps, for example facing them so they can lip-read.
source_name: UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities

statement: The UAE uses the term 'People of Determination' for people with disabilities.
explanation_short: In the UAE, people with disabilities are called People of Determination.
explanation_long: The UAE adopted the term 'People of Determination' to recognise the achievements of people with disabilities.

statement: Accommodations give students an unfair advantage.
explanation_short: Accommodations remove barriers; they don't add advantages.
explanation_long: An accommodation changes how a student shows what they know, not what they need to know, so everyone is assessed on the same skills.
source_name: UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities

statement: Extra exam time is a common academic accommodation.
explanation_short: Extended time is one of the most common accommodations.
explanation_long: Extra time helps students who process information or write more slowly due to a disability show their real knowledge.
source_name: UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities

statement: You need a visible disability to get accommodations.
explanation_short: Invisible disabilities can qualify for accommodations too.
explanation_long: Accommodations are based on need, including for ADHD, dyslexia, anxiety, chronic illness and other invisible conditions.
source_name: UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities

statement: Accommodations lower the standards a student has to meet.
explanation_short: The standards stay the same.
explanation_long: Reasonable accommodations adjust the conditions, like time, format or setting, while the course standards and learning goals stay the same.
source_name: UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities

statement: Students get to decide whether to share their disability with classmates.
explanation_short: Disability information is private.
explanation_long: A student's disability information is personal and private. It's their choice whether and who to tell.
source_name: UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities

statement: Captions on videos help many people, not only Deaf viewers.
explanation_short: Captions help everyone: noisy rooms, second languages, focus.
explanation_long: Captions help Deaf and hard-of-hearing people, and also people watching in noisy places, non-native speakers and anyone who focuses better with text.

statement: Professors should announce in class which students have accommodations.
explanation_short: Accommodations should be kept confidential.
explanation_long: Accommodations should be handled privately between the student, the instructor and the support office.
source_name: UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities

statement: Asking for support early in the semester gives the most time to set it up.
explanation_short: Ask early so support is ready when you need it.
explanation_long: Some accommodations, like exam arrangements or materials in other formats, take time to organise, so it's best to reach out early.

statement: Quiet spaces and short breaks can help students with sensory sensitivities.
explanation_short: Small changes to the environment can make a big difference.
explanation_long: Noise, light and crowds can be overwhelming for some neurodivergent students. Quiet spaces and breaks help them stay focused and comfortable.

statement: Once you have an accommodation, it can never be changed.
explanation_short: Accommodations can be reviewed as needs change.
explanation_long: Needs can change over time or between courses. Students can ask to review or update their accommodations.
